To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned and characterized the first MC receptors from agnathans.
we have identified two melanocortine receptors in lamprey that show orthology to the melanocortine receptor subtypes MC1 and MC 4.

we have identified two ancestral MC receptors from riverlamprey, which showed orthology to MC1 and MC 4 receptor subtypes and were able to bind and to be activated by both human and lamprey MSH peptides.

evolution of melanocortins and their receptors in the vertebrates.
the evolution and functional characterization of MC receptors in lamprey.
the evolution of melanocortins in the context of GPCR evolution and the role of GPCRs in the control of body weight.

lamprey MCa and MC4 receptors show orthology to MC1 and MC3 receptor subtypes, and lamprey MCa has affinity for ACTH peptides similarly to fish MC1 and MC2 receptors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MC receptors are present and have similar function to the MC4 receptor in lamprey, and that the MC1 receptor has been lost in lamprey.
the lamprey receptors have a high affinity for ACTHR and MSH peptides and the MCa receptor is the ancestral MC1-like subtype, while the MC receptor is ancestral MC4-like subtype.
lamprey MCa and MC4 receptors have retained their ancestral functions, but they have diverged from each another.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MC1 and the MC4 receptors have been present in agnathan species for a long time and have been involved in regulating pigmentation and energy homeostasis.
lamprey MCa receptors are activated by both lampreys and human MSH and ACTH derived peptides and thus may have a role in regulating body color.
the ancestral lamprey MC receptors are able to bind and signal to the human MSH and ACTH peptides.
